critical_issues.issue: User-provided pantry and expiration data may be inaccurate or incomplete
critical_issues.why_it_matters: Inaccurate inputs lead to irrelevant or unsafe meal suggestions, undermining trust and potentially increasing waste

critical_issues.issue: Generated meal suggestions may not be appealing or practical for users
critical_issues.why_it_matters: If users reject the suggestions, the system fails to influence behavior, rendering the intervention ineffective

critical_issues.issue: Measuring food waste before and after the intervention is challenging
critical_issues.why_it_matters: Without reliable measurement, any claimed reduction in waste cannot be validated, compromising the study's conclusions

fragile_assumptions: Users know what ingredients they have at home
Users can estimate or have access to approximate expiration dates
Users are willing to input pantry data into the system
The generated suggestions are practical and appealing enough to be followed
Food waste can be measured before and after the intervention
failure_modes: User fatigue leading to abandonment of data entry
Privacy concerns causing users to withhold ingredient information
Algorithmic bias producing repetitive or culturally irrelevant meals
System overload if many users submit large pantry inventories
missing_information: Actual willingness of target users to regularly update pantry data
Baseline food waste quantities for the target demographic
Details on the algorithmic approach for matching ingredients to recipes
Integration plan with existing grocery or pantry management apps
User onboarding and education strategy to ensure correct data entry
overclaims: The system will definitively reduce food waste without accounting for external factors such as shopping habits or price incentives
